personal_bio: Marilisa Allegrini is an Italian wine entrepreneur known as “Lady Amarone” for her role in promoting Valpolicella wines worldwide. With over four decades of experience, she leads the Marilisa Allegrini Group alongside her daughters, Carlotta and Caterina, bringing together three prestigious estates: Villa Della Torre, Poggio al Tesoro and San Polo. In 2020, she was awarded the title of Cavaliere del Lavoro in recognition of her contribution to Italian business.
company_bio: Founded in 2024, Marilisa Allegrini Group is a family-owned Italian wine company led by Marilisa Allegrini alongside her daughters, Carlotta and Caterina. Bringing together Villa Della Torre in Veneto and Poggio al Tesoro and San Polo in Tuscany, the group combines winemaking, hospitality and a passion for art, celebrating the character and traditions of each territory.
general_bio: Marilisa Allegrini, known as “Lady Amarone,” is an Italian wine entrepreneur with over four decades of experience promoting Italian wines worldwide. Alongside her daughters, Carlotta and Caterina, she leads the Marilisa Allegrini Group, uniting Villa Della Torre in Veneto with Poggio al Tesoro and San Polo in Tuscany through a shared passion for wine, art and hospitality.

personal_bio: Micaela Pallini is an Italian entrepreneur and President and CEO of Pallini S.p.A., representing the fifth generation of her family’s historic spirits company. Trained in chemistry, she combines scientific expertise with a passion for Italian liqueurs, supporting product innovation and international growth. She served as President of Federvini from 2021 to 2025 and was named Cavaliere del Lavoro in 2026.
company_bio: Pallini S.p.A. is a family-owned Italian spirits company founded in 1875 and based in Rome. Best known for Pallini Limoncello, it also produces traditional liqueurs, including Mistrà and Sambuca, alongside a range of syrups. Led by fifth-generation President and CEO Micaela Pallini, the company combines a longstanding family heritage with innovation and an international presence.
general_bio: Micaela Pallini is President and CEO of Pallini S.p.A., a family-owned Italian spirits company founded in 1875 and based in Rome. Representing the fifth generation, she combines her background in chemistry with a passion for Italian craftsmanship, guiding the company behind the renowned Pallini Limoncello through innovation and international growth.

personal_bio: Nadia Zenato is an Italian wine entrepreneur and co-owner of her family’s winery, which she leads alongside her brother, Alberto. Responsible for marketing, communications and international development, she promotes the wines of Lugana and Valpolicella worldwide while carrying forward the legacy of her parents, Sergio and Carla Zenato.
company_bio: Zenato is a family-owned Italian winery founded in 1960 by Sergio Zenato and Carla Prospero near Lake Garda. Known for its Lugana, Amarone della Valpolicella and Ripassa wines, the company combines respect for local grape varieties with a commitment to quality and innovation. Today, Nadia and Alberto Zenato carry forward their parents’ legacy, sharing the character of their wine regions with audiences worldwide.
general_bio: Nadia Zenato is an Italian wine entrepreneur who leads Zenato alongside her brother, Alberto. Founded by their parents in 1960 near Lake Garda, the family winery is known for its Lugana, Amarone and Ripassa wines. Nadia oversees marketing and international development, sharing her family’s winemaking heritage with audiences worldwide.

personal_bio: Chiara Lungarotti is an Italian wine entrepreneur and CEO of her family’s winery, Lungarotti, in Umbria. A graduate in agriculture with a specialisation in viticulture, she has led the company since 1999. Her work combines innovation, sustainability and respect for tradition, carrying forward her father Giorgio’s legacy and her deep connection to the region.
company_bio: Lungarotti is a family-owned Italian winery founded by Giorgio Lungarotti in the early 1960s in Torgiano, Umbria. Today, under the leadership of Chiara Lungarotti, the company combines its winemaking heritage with innovation and sustainable practices, celebrating the region’s character through its wines and its commitment to wine culture and hospitality.
general_bio: Chiara Lungarotti is an Italian wine entrepreneur and CEO of Lungarotti, the family winery founded by her father Giorgio in Torgiano, Umbria, in the early 1960s. Trained in agriculture and viticulture, she has led the company since 1999, combining innovation and sustainability with a commitment to her family’s winemaking heritage and the region’s traditions.

personal_bio: Marina Cvetić is a wine entrepreneur who leads Masciarelli Tenute Agricole in Abruzzo alongside her daughter, Miriam Lee. After building the business with her husband, Gianni Masciarelli, she continued its development following his death in 2008. Her work has helped bring the region’s wines to international audiences while strengthening the family’s commitment to hospitality and its local heritage.
company_bio: Masciarelli Tenute Agricole is an Abruzzo wine producer founded by Gianni Masciarelli in 1981 and based in San Martino sulla Marrucina. Its vineyards span the region’s four provinces, with wines including Montepulciano d’Abruzzo and Trebbiano d’Abruzzo. The family business also produces olive oil and welcomes guests at Castello di Semivicoli.
general_bio: Marina Cvetić leads Masciarelli Tenute Agricole alongside her daughter, Miriam Lee, continuing the work she began with Gianni Masciarelli. Based in Abruzzo, the family winery is known for its Montepulciano and Trebbiano wines, combining regional identity with international reach and wine tourism at Castello di Semivicoli.

personal_bio: Miriam Lee Masciarelli is a wine entrepreneur and brand ambassador who helps lead her family’s Abruzzo winery alongside her mother, Marina Cvetić. The eldest daughter of founder Gianni Masciarelli, she represents the next generation of the business. Her work includes promoting its wines internationally and developing projects that connect wine, contemporary art and hospitality.
company_bio: Masciarelli Tenute Agricole is a family wine business based in San Martino sulla Marrucina, Abruzzo. Founded in 1981, it produces wines from estate vineyards across the region, including its Villa Gemma and Marina Cvetić collections. Its activities also encompass olive oil, wine distribution and hospitality at Castello di Semivicoli.
general_bio: Miriam Lee Masciarelli represents the next generation of Masciarelli Tenute Agricole, the Abruzzo winery founded by her father, Gianni. Working with her mother, Marina Cvetić, she shares the family’s wines with international audiences and brings contemporary art and hospitality into its continuing story.

personal_bio: Roberta Bricolo leads Gorgo, the family winery established by her parents, Alberta and Roberto, in Custoza. Originally trained as a lawyer, she returned to the family’s winemaking roots and began converting its vineyards to organic farming in 2014. Her approach focuses on regional grape varieties and wines that express the landscape between Verona and Lake Garda.
company_bio: Gorgo is a family winery founded in 1975 in Custoza, near Verona and Lake Garda. Led by Roberta Bricolo, it cultivates certified organic vineyards and produces wines rooted in the area’s traditions, including Custoza, Bardolino and Chiaretto. The estate combines local varieties with a focus on sustainable vineyard management.
general_bio: Roberta Bricolo is the proprietor of Gorgo, the Custoza winery founded by her parents in 1975. A former lawyer, she has guided its transition to organic viticulture, producing wines that reflect the grape varieties and landscape of the area between Verona and Lake Garda.

personal_bio: Alicia Lini represents the fourth generation of her family’s Lini 910 winery in Correggio, Emilia-Romagna. She promotes the family’s wines internationally, helping introduce audiences to the diversity and quality of Lambrusco. Her work carries forward a winemaking tradition that dates to her great-grandfather Oreste’s founding of the business in 1910.
company_bio: Lini 910 is a family winery founded by Oreste Lini in Correggio in 1910. Rooted in Emilia-Romagna’s Lambrusco tradition, it produces sparkling wines using both tank and traditional bottle-fermentation methods. The family’s activities also include traditional balsamic vinegar from Reggio Emilia.
general_bio: Alicia Lini is the fourth-generation representative of Lini 910, her family’s historic winery in Correggio. Founded in 1910, the estate is dedicated to Lambrusco and sparkling wines. Alicia shares this Emilian heritage internationally, highlighting the variety and craftsmanship behind the family’s production.

personal_bio: Giovanna Caponi leads Le Palaie, the wine estate and agriturismo created by her father, Nino Angelo Caponi, in Tuscany’s Alta Valdera. She took over following his death in 2020, bringing experience from the family’s logistics business. Working with a team of trusted collaborators, she continues his commitment to wine, agriculture and welcoming visitors.
company_bio: Le Palaie is a family estate in Peccioli, Tuscany, established by Nino Angelo Caponi in 1996. The property combines vineyards, olive groves and woodland with a winery, accommodation and event spaces. Its wines and hospitality reflect the landscape of Alta Valdera and the Caponi family’s attachment to the area.
general_bio: Giovanna Caponi leads Le Palaie in Peccioli, continuing the estate founded by her father, Nino, in 1996. The Tuscan property brings together wine production, olive growing and agriturismo. Giovanna carries forward its family identity through a close relationship with the land and a focus on hospitality.

personal_bio: Filomena Iacobucci helps lead Terre Stregate, her family’s wine and olive-oil business in Guardia Sanframondi, Campania, alongside her brother, Carlo. A graduate in economics from LUISS, she has contributed to the company’s commercial development and international growth. Her work promotes the Sannio region and its distinctive grape varieties.
company_bio: Terre Stregate is a family wine and olive-oil producer in Guardia Sanframondi, in Campania’s Sannio area. The Iacobucci family traces its agricultural roots to 1898. Its range includes wines from Falanghina, Aglianico, Fiano and Greco, combining regional varieties with the family’s longstanding farming tradition.
general_bio: Filomena Iacobucci represents the Iacobucci family at Terre Stregate in Campania’s Sannio region. Working alongside her brother, Carlo, she supports the development of a business rooted in wine and olive oil, bringing its Falanghina and other regional wines to a wider audience.

personal_bio: Chiara Abbona is part of the family team behind Marziano Abbona in Dogliani, Piedmont. The youngest daughter of Marziano, she joined the business alongside her sister, Mara, continuing the values passed down by their grandfather, Celso. Her work supports the winery’s combination of regional tradition, experimentation and a closer relationship with wine lovers.
company_bio: Marziano Abbona is a family winery based in Dogliani in Piedmont’s Langhe region. Its identity is closely associated with Dolcetto, particularly Papà Celso, alongside wines from Nebbiolo, Barbera and other varieties. Marziano and his daughters carry forward a tradition of careful vineyard work while exploring new styles and welcoming visitors.
general_bio: Chiara Abbona works alongside her family at Marziano Abbona, the Dogliani winery known for Papà Celso and its broader range of Langhe wines. Together with her father and sister, Mara, she continues the family’s dedication to its vineyards while bringing a new generation’s perspective to the business.

personal_bio: Francesca Paladin represents the third generation of Casa Paladin, her family’s wine group. Working alongside her cousins and other family members, she is involved in the development and international promotion of its estates. Her approach connects regional winemaking traditions with the group’s sustainability programme and a commitment to sharing its family heritage.
company_bio: Casa Paladin is a family wine group whose origins date to 1962. Its portfolio includes Paladin, Bosco del Merlo, Casa Lupo, Castello Bonomi and Castelvecchi, spanning Veneto, Friuli, Franciacorta and Tuscany. The group combines the distinct identities of its estates with shared work on viticulture, quality and sustainability.
general_bio: Francesca Paladin is part of the third generation guiding Casa Paladin, a family wine group with estates across several Italian regions. Through its diverse portfolio, she promotes the relationship between wine and place while supporting international growth and the family’s commitment to sustainability.

personal_bio: Maria Faretra is a wine entrepreneur associated with her namesake winery in Orta Nova, in northern Puglia. She represents a female-led business committed to organic production and the preservation of its local heritage. Her work introduces the wines of Capitanata to international audiences, with particular attention to the region’s grape varieties and biodiversity.
company_bio: Maria Faretra Wines is a female-led producer based in Orta Nova in Puglia’s Capitanata region. The company focuses on limited-production organic wines, including Nero di Troia, Primitivo and Malbech. Its approach combines vineyard heritage with contemporary presentation and a commitment to biodiversity and reduced environmental impact.
general_bio: Maria Faretra represents her namesake wine business in northern Puglia, sharing the character of Capitanata through organic wines. Based in Orta Nova, the female-led producer works with Nero di Troia, Primitivo and Malbech, combining local heritage with a contemporary approach to wine and sustainability.

personal_bio: Natalie Oliveros is the American-born owner of La Fiorita in Montalcino, Tuscany. Raised with an Italian family heritage, she developed an early connection to wine through home winemaking. At La Fiorita, she works with the estate team to explore different expressions of Sangiovese, including the parcel-selected Brunello Fiore di NO and Ninfalia rosé.
company_bio: La Fiorita is a wine estate in Montalcino, Tuscany, owned by Natalie Oliveros. Its production centres on Sangiovese and the distinctive soils of its vineyards, with a portfolio including Brunello di Montalcino and the Fiore di NO selection. The estate also produces Ninfalia, a rosé fermented in concrete eggs.
general_bio: Natalie Oliveros owns La Fiorita, the Montalcino estate dedicated to expressing the diversity of Sangiovese. Drawing on her Italian family heritage, she works with the winery team on Brunello di Montalcino and wines such as Fiore di NO and Ninfalia, giving a personal direction to the estate’s production.

personal_bio: Annamaria Sorricchio di Valforte represents the next generation of her family’s Barone di Valforte estate in Abruzzo. With a background in law and further business education, she joined the family’s winegrowing and winemaking activities. Alongside her father, Guido, and uncle, Francesco, she helps carry forward the estate’s heritage and connection to the region.
company_bio: Barone di Valforte is a family wine estate in Abruzzo, between the Adriatic Sea and the Gran Sasso mountains. The property has belonged to the Sorricchio di Valforte family since the fourteenth century. Its wines include Montepulciano, Trebbiano and Cerasuolo d’Abruzzo, supported by sustainable farming and a commitment to preserving local identity.
general_bio: Annamaria Sorricchio di Valforte continues her family’s wine heritage at Barone di Valforte in Abruzzo. Working with her father and uncle, she contributes to an estate whose history stretches back centuries and whose production focuses on regional wines and respect for the surrounding environment.

personal_bio: Elena Fucci is a winemaker and proprietor in Barile, Basilicata. In 2000, she chose to preserve her family’s vineyards rather than see them sold, establishing the winery that bears her name. Trained in viticulture and oenology at the University of Pisa, she is known for Titolo, her expression of Aglianico grown on the slopes of Mount Vulture.
company_bio: Azienda Agricola Elena Fucci was established in 2000 in Barile, Basilicata, around family vineyards in Contrada Solagna del Titolo. The estate focuses on Aglianico del Vulture and its volcanic growing environment. Its Titolo range expresses the character of these vineyards through different selections and approaches to ageing.
general_bio: Elena Fucci is the winemaker behind her namesake estate in Barile, Basilicata. Founded in 2000 to continue her family’s vineyard tradition, the winery is closely associated with Titolo and Aglianico del Vulture. Elena combines her technical training with a commitment to the distinctive landscape of Mount Vulture.

personal_bio: Chiara Soldati is the owner and CEO of La Scolca in Gavi, Piedmont, representing the fourth generation of her family’s wine business. She has led the winery since 1998, promoting its wines internationally and developing its hospitality offering. In 2022, she was awarded the title of Cavaliere del Lavoro for her contribution to Italian enterprise.
company_bio: La Scolca is a historic family winery in Gavi, Piedmont, with a winemaking heritage dating to 1919. Known for its Cortese-based Gavi wines, including Gavi dei Gavi Etichetta Nera, it also produces traditional-method sparkling wines. Under Chiara Soldati’s leadership, the estate combines international distribution with wine tourism.
general_bio: Chiara Soldati leads La Scolca, her family’s historic Gavi winery, as owner and CEO. A fourth-generation entrepreneur and Cavaliere del Lavoro, she promotes the estate’s Cortese wines and sparkling cuvées worldwide, continuing a family tradition that dates to 1919.

personal_bio: Francesca Mecchia represents the third generation of women at Vigna Petrussa in Prepotto, Friuli-Venezia Giulia. Trained as an architect, she joined her mother, Hilde Petrussa, in the family winery, bringing a new perspective to its image and development. She continues a tradition begun by her grandmother, Giuseppina, with a particular attachment to Schioppettino and the local landscape.
company_bio: Vigna Petrussa is a family winery in Prepotto, in the Colli Orientali del Friuli, shaped by three generations of women. Led by Hilde Petrussa and Francesca Mecchia, it places particular emphasis on native grapes, including Schioppettino. Its vineyards grow on the area’s characteristic marl soils, known as ponca.
general_bio: Francesca Mecchia works alongside her mother, Hilde Petrussa, at Vigna Petrussa in Prepotto. Bringing her architectural background to the family business, she represents its third generation of women. The winery celebrates Friuli’s native varieties, especially Schioppettino, and the identity of its hillside vineyards.

personal_bio: Francesca Bardelli Nonino represents the sixth generation of the Nonino family in Friuli. With a background in business economics, she works in communication and international markets for the family distillery. Known as the “grappa influencer,” she uses digital storytelling to introduce younger audiences to grappa and explain the craft behind its production.
company_bio: Nonino Distillatori is a family spirits producer in Percoto, Friuli-Venezia Giulia, with a tradition dating to 1897. In 1973, Benito and Giannola Nonino pioneered the company’s Monovitigno grappa by distilling Picolit pomace separately. Its range includes grappa, grape distillates and Amaro Nonino, produced with an emphasis on artisanal distillation.
general_bio: Francesca Bardelli Nonino brings a sixth-generation perspective to Nonino Distillatori, her family’s historic Friulian spirits business. Through international work and digital communication, she shares the culture of grappa with new audiences, connecting contemporary storytelling with a distilling tradition established in 1897.

personal_bio: Barbara Galassi, co-owns Cantina Paltrinieri with her husband, Alberto. They began managing the family winery together in 1998, focusing on Lambrusco di Sorbara. Her work contributes to a family business whose identity centres on careful production and a strong attachment to its home in Sorbara.
company_bio: Cantina Paltrinieri is a family winery in Sorbara, near Modena, founded by Achille Paltrinieri in 1926. It specialises in Lambrusco di Sorbara and cultivates vineyards in the historic Cristo area between the Secchia and Panaro rivers. Alberto Paltrinieri and Barbara Galassi lead the business, with the next generation involved.
general_bio: Barbara Galassi co-owns Cantina Paltrinieri in Sorbara with her husband, Alberto. Since taking over in 1998, they have continued the winery’s focus on Lambrusco di Sorbara and its local vineyards, carrying forward a family tradition established in 1926.

personal_bio: Cecilia Paltrinieri is part of the next generation at her family’s Cantina Paltrinieri in Sorbara, near Modena. The daughter of Alberto and Barbara, she is responsible for hospitality at the winery. Through welcoming visitors and sharing the family’s story, she helps introduce its Lambrusco wines and local traditions to new audiences.
company_bio: Cantina Paltrinieri is a family producer of Lambrusco di Sorbara with roots dating to 1926. Based in the Cristo area of Sorbara, it is led by Alberto Paltrinieri and Barbara Galassi, with their children contributing to the business. The winery combines a focus on its local grape with visitor hospitality.
general_bio: Cecilia Paltrinieri oversees hospitality at Cantina Paltrinieri, her family’s Lambrusco winery in Sorbara. Representing a new generation alongside her parents, Alberto and Barbara, she welcomes visitors and shares the story of a wine business rooted in the Modena area since 1926.
